completion_data.completion_summary: Added a new 'The Token's Durable Homes and the Never-Copy Boundary' subsection to per-repo-scoping.md, backed by a verified by-value (not by-filename) re-check of all four candidate token locations, which found that the sf1-hub-ben copies match the currently-active config.json token rather than being a different credential as the plan guessed, while the sops-provisioned secret (/run/secrets/sapience_token) has diverged from that active token -- both findings stated honestly in the doc and recorded via issue-record.sh. Confirmed secrets.yaml remains the sole git-tracked location and is sops-encrypted. Bumped index-entries.json's line_count and keywords for the edited doc.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience token: sops secret vs. active config.json token
sapience_notes.value: On this machine, the token ~/.sapience/config.json's .token field currently holds (the one mcp.py actually authenticates with) does NOT match the value in /run/secrets/sapience_token (the sops-nix provisioned secret) -- they differ in both length and content. config.json's oldest backup (config.json.bak-20261103-175726) matches the sops secret; its two newer backups match the currently-active value. The two credentials have diverged, most likely via a manual token rotation applied to config.json that was never mirrored back into ~/.dotfiles/secrets/secrets.yaml. Reconciling them is a ~/.dotfiles-owned action.

sapience_notes.subject: sf1-hub-ben's token files hold the SAME credential as config.json, not a different one
sapience_notes.value: A by-value fingerprint comparison (length + sha256[:12], never the raw value) showed ~/.config/sf1-hub-ben/env's SAPIENCE_TOKEN and ~/.config/sf1-hub-ben/sapience-token are byte-identical to the token ~/.sapience/config.json currently resolves -- contradicting an earlier guess (based only on differing file sizes against /run/secrets/sapience_token) that sf1-hub-ben's copy was a different credential for a different subsystem. Filename/byte-size similarity to the WRONG reference file produced the wrong inference; comparing against the actually-relevant reference (config.json's active token) settled it correctly.

sapience_notes.subject: sf1-hub-ben credential files are manually populated, not nix-declared
sapience_notes.value: ~/.config/sf1-hub-ben/env and ~/.config/sf1-hub-ben/sapience-token are populated by hand via the `sf1-hub-ben token` CLI subcommand, not by home-manager activation -- the sf1-hub-ben.nix module's own documented policy is that nothing granting consent or holding a credential belongs in an activation script. ~/.dotfiles's sf1-hub-ben module owns the directory's packaging/existence, but not the file contents, which the module deliberately never touches.

sapience_notes.subject: A measurement record's own recorded fingerprint can itself be wrong
sapience_notes.value: A prior phase's record file stated ~/.sapience/config.json's .token SHA-256[:12] fingerprint as 1ccd05e02475; independently recomputing the same field on the same, unmodified file (confirmed via unchanged mtime) a few hours later yielded a different fingerprint (20a5377da89a) at the same string length. The file was not touched between the two measurements, so the earlier record's fingerprint value was itself mistranscribed -- a reminder that even a 'measured, not assumed' record can carry a transcription error in its own output, and that a later phase re-deriving the same fact independently (rather than trusting the earlier record's stated value) is what caught it.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh's OWED fallback battery and a known deploy-staleness failure
sapience_notes.value: Running verify-touched.sh with no arguments against a touched set that includes a specs/** progress/metadata file (alongside a clean extension-scoped edit) triggers BOTH the extension-scoped battery (narrow, selected suites) AND a second, root-scoped 'OWED fallback' battery (98 suites) when some touched path cannot be mapped to a specific extension/suite. The root-scoped fallback ran in ~310s and is cheap to run detached with a bounded kill -0 wait rather than a bare foreground call that a tool-call ceiling could abandon mid-run.
